commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Add feature freeze and docs guidance
commitResults.messageBody:
The project is now in the v1.6 feature freeze, so agents need to
know the src/main line limit and to focus on bugs, error messages,
the UG, the DG, and UML diagrams.

* Add the freeze dates, line limit, and bug triage steps
* Add rules for short, consistent error messages
* Add guidance on keeping the UG and DG concise and fixing UML

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Update outdated code references
commitResults.messageBody:
Several examples no longer matched the code: find was replaced by
filter, duplicate detection now normalizes names and checks school
and level, and the name rule is now a documented team decision.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Add this semester's PE and submission rules
commitResults.messageBody: The course dropped the PE dry run, the Planned Enhancements appendix, and PDF documents this semester. Record the rules that replace them so agents do not follow past semesters' pages.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Cover all PE bug categories
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide missed several bug types from the tP grading page, such as
extra parameters, hard-to-test features, UG visuals, and DG user
stories, use cases, NFRs, glossary, and diagram choice.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Add DG reader and Effort appendix rules
commitResults.messageBody:
PE testers judge the DG as a new team member would, and read
Appendix: Effort before estimating the team's implementation effort.

commitResults.messageTitle: AGENTS.md: Limit when error messages share text
commitResults.messageBody:
Merging messages that only look alike can make one field's message
wrong, and every refactor uses up freeze lines.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Convert glossary to tables
Developer Guide: Convert glossary to tables
AGENTS.md: Keep issue and PR descriptions short
Developer Guide: Add effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
Evaluators read this appendix to estimate the team's implementation
effort relative to AB3. It covers the difficulty, challenges, measured
code growth, fixes to diagrams inherited from AB3, achievements, and
reused code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Count effort lines with RepoSense
commitResults.messageBody:
Use the RepoSense functional-code counts that graders see, instead of
git line counts. These credit only lines the team wrote, and include
FXML and CSS files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add process figures to effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
Lines of code show only a lower bound on effort, largely because of
AI coding tools. Add issue, pull request, and alpha-testing bug counts
as a better indication.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Refine AB3 diagram fixes in effort
commitResults.messageBody:
Mention that AB3's parser class diagram also showed a ParserUtil
dependency on Prefix that never existed, and clarify how the team
handled the PlantUML lifeline limitation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Revise achievements in effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
The section listed features already described under difficulty.
Replace it with outcomes evaluators can check: shared field rules,
specific error messages, and test coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Separate non-implementation effort
commitResults.messageBody:
Evaluators are told to count implementation work only. Move project
management, testing, and documentation work into its own section, and
count only code bugs as evidence of implementation effort.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add AB3 flaw fixes to effort challenges
commitResults.messageBody:
Before adding features, the team audited AB3 and logged 37 problems.
Several needed code fixes, which count as implementation effort but
were missing from the appendix.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Explain why effort challenges were hard
commitResults.messageBody:
The challenges described what was built, not why it was difficult.
Explain the competing goals, the alternatives weighed, and the
disagreements the team resolved for each one.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Note that effort line counts may differ
Developer Guide: Avoid dated bug counts in effort
commitResults.messageBody:
The counts of open and fixed alpha-testing bugs would need updating
after v1.6. State the number fixed instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Avoid dated counts beyond implementation
commitResults.messageBody:
The issue, pull request, test, and bug counts would need updating
after v1.6. State lower bounds instead, which stay true as they grow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Soften claims about effort measures
Developer Guide: Tighten effort line count paragraphs
Developer Guide: Broaden better effort indication
commitResults.messageBody:
Besides bug fixes, mention design discussions and revisions made in
response to review, which are also implementation work. List them as
bullets for readability.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Mention code review in effort appendix
Developer Guide: Fix inaccuracies in effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
AB3's fields are classes, not plain strings, and only subjects,
guardians, and notes have JSON adapters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Tighten effort appendix and add links
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a summary sentence, link each challenge to its pull requests so
evaluators can check it, and trim repeated content toward the one-page
guideline.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Shorten effort appendix further
commitResults.messageBody:
Condense the work outside implementation and remove repeated points,
bringing the appendix closer to the one-page guideline.
